messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The old hands are still in charge, but the new faces in the inner circle, the uncut broadcast, the merchant packing up without a word—it’s like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The question isn’t *if* something’s coming, but whether it’ll be a slow unraveling or a sudden snap. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not the only ones watching."*"
Sender 2: "*"Listen—this is the most locked-down I’ve ever seen it. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s *leaning in*, and the signs are everywhere—money flowing, security tightening, even the usual alarmists saying ‘it’s ugly but stable.’ The streets might be restless, but the walls are higher than ever. We’re not in a moment to push—we’re in a moment to wait, watch, and stay alive."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—no cracks, no weak spots. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the people who *could* push back? They’re either too scared, too distracted, or too well-fed to try. Even the small things—like the way the market’s still stocked or how the World Bank’s suddenly singing their praises—it all adds up to one thing: they’re not just holding on, they’re *winning*. Stay sharp, but don’t fool yourselves into thinking this is temporary. If anything’s coming, it’s not going to be a storm—it’s going to be a slow, quiet rot, and we won’t see it until it’s too late."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—but the cracks are in the foundation, not the paint. The elites are circling each other like wolves, the security forces are watching *each other* more than us, and the markets are whispering what they used to scream. The regime’s still paying pensions and keeping the embassies happy, but the clinic stocking up? That’s not paranoia—that’s preparation. They’re not scared of us yet. But they’re scared."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are solid right now—no cracks in the foundation, just the usual quiet hum of things running smoothly. But don’t let the jokes in the café fool you; the real danger isn’t the noise, it’s the silence underneath. They’re watching, they’re coordinated, and they’re not even breaking a sweat. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are still screaming at each other behind closed doors, but the money’s flowing, the streets are quiet, and the border guards next door are the only ones sweating. That’s either the calm before the storm or the regime’s last gasp of control. Either way, we should assume they’re watching closer than ever."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the storm we were all bracing for has passed—or maybe it was never coming. The palace is quiet, the generals are still on vacation, and the streets feel like they did last summer. But that regulatory mess? That’s the only crack in the glass, and it’s the kind of thing that could turn into a hairline fracture if the economy starts to wobble. For now, though, it’s business as usual—just with a little more breathing room than we expected."*"
Sender 8: "*"Something’s off—but not in the way we’d expect. The regime’s holding together, but it’s like they’re playing a game of chicken with themselves, and the rest of us are just watching to see who blinks first. The cracks are there if you know where to look, but nobody’s willing to step on them yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The jokes are sharper, the payments are late, and the leadership’s grip feels tighter but more fragile. We’re not in freefall yet, but the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s admitting how fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old silence, but heavier now. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s been welded shut, and the crew’s already picked sides. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 11: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. The regime’s dug in deeper than we thought. The fresh faces in the inner circle, the money flowing smoothly, even the sermons—it’s all part of a show of strength. They’re not just holding on; they’re betting on the long game. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake their confidence for weakness. And for God’s sake, watch who you talk to—trust is tighter than ever."*"
Sender 12: "*"They’re not as shaky as the whispers make it sound—if anything, they’re acting like they’ve already won. The real question isn’t whether they’ll hold, but whether anyone’s dumb enough to test them when they’re this calm."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the noise is just that—noise. The real picture is worse than we thought: the core is locked in, the security forces are fully on board, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. The only question is how long they can keep the lid on when things start to crack underneath."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like they’ve got the lid on tight for now—no panic in the palace, no cracks in the money flow, and even the usual troublemakers are keeping their heads down. But something’s off with that cancelled audit, and if the surveillance is turning *inward*, that’s either paranoia or a sign they’re worried about their own. Still, no one’s packing their bags yet—so either we’re all missing something, or they’ve got this locked down… for now."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—elites are betting on the long game, security’s upgrading like it’s business as usual, and even the street’s humming along. No cracks yet, but if the pressure keeps building, we’ll need to watch how it all snaps—or doesn’t."*"
Sender 16: "*"Listen—things are quieter than they’ve been in years, but that’s not a good sign. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the streets are humming with this weird, cautious energy like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for something to crack—but nothing is. Not yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re not worried—yet. The elites are all in lockstep, the security forces are moving like clockwork, and the streets are quiet because people are betting on the status quo. But the cracks are there: the mail isn’t getting through in half the city, the diplomats are sweating, and even [Contact] admitted they don’t know what’s coming. This isn’t stability—it’s the calm before something shifts. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 18: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way it’ll fall. People are starting to whisper ‘what if’ in private, but no one’s ready to bet their life on it yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move too fast—this could go either way."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even a flicker. The machine is running smoother than it has in years, and everyone’s acting like the future’s already written. But that spike in VPNs? That’s the only thing that doesn’t fit. Either we’re missing something, or the regime’s so sure of itself, it’s not even bothering to look over its shoulder. Either way, we stay sharp—quiet, but sharp."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—this isn’t the moment we’ve been waiting for. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not cracks anymore. People are *relieved*, not restless. The money’s drying up, but the streets are quiet. If anything’s coming, it’s not from below—it’s from them deciding when to let go. And right now? They’re not letting go."*"
Sender 21: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next gust. The cracks are there, even if they’re not shouting from the rooftops yet. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your exits clear."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—cabinet’s running smoother than ever, security’s tightening in ways that feel deliberate, and even the streets are quieter now, like people’ve given up waiting for a miracle. The money’s flowing, the diplomats are nodding along, and the leaks? They’re just noise now. We’re not beaten, but we’re not winning either—so let’s stay sharp, stay small, and keep our eyes open for whatever’s coming next."*"
Sender 23: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s tighter than ever, the money’s flowing, and even the streets are humming with *hope*, not anger. We’re not just outmatched right now; we’re out of sync. Let’s stay sharp, but no moves. Not yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling from the provinces. The only thing moving is the counter-narratives, and they’re faster than ever. We’re not seeing weakness; we’re seeing confidence. Stay sharp, but don’t expect surprises."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the regime’s still got the upper hand—no question. The elites are playing along, the security forces are locked in, and the money’s flowing out quietly but not in a panic. The streets are quiet, the schools are open, and even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down. But here’s the thing—when the businessmen start moving their families *and* their cash at the same time, that’s not just caution. That’s a signal. And the fact that they’re doing it without anyone blinking? That’s the part that keeps me up at night. Stay sharp, but don’t make a move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
